parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, entry-document regime, facility ban, or police targeting of visitors is documented, and national law covers gender-identity discrimination with transphobia as an aggravating factor. The operative exposure is custody: trans women are placed by legal marker in practice in all-male facilities facing assault threats, and the 2021 watchdog found persistence of serious violations across all places of deprivation of liberty, with no documented remedy or local inspection. That conditional tier-1 custody exposure, unresolved for this collectivity, outweighs the paper protections.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Placement by legal gender marker in practice means trans women in all-male facilities facing detainee assault threats; watchdog found persistence of serious violations across all detention places.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Detention watchdog inspected mainland establishments and made referrals on about 40 transgender persons since 2010, but no remedy for the documented pattern is shown.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any visitor detention or transfer into the national prison system applies the same placement practice; no local inspection or follow-up is documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No visitor bathroom, ward, or public-facility restriction is documented.

care_services.exposure: A 2022 care report found lack of self-determination, extended waits and inequitable access in the governing state; no visitor-specific denial or medication seizure is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No criminalisation of gender expression, cross-dressing or presentation, and no police targeting of visitors, is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Gender-identity discrimination is a penal-code ground since 2016 wording update, and transphobic motive has been an aggravating factor for imprisonable crimes since 2017, applying here as national law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: These protections are documented nationally; they do not documentably remedy the custody placements described.

minors_guardians.exposure: A May 2024 senate bill to ban medical transition under 18 was documented with no update after 23 July 2024 and described as unlikely to pass; no operative visitor or guardian rule is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Unresolved bill status creates uncertainty, not a documented operative restriction for travelling minors or guardians.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police recorded about 1,870 homophobic and transphobic attack victims nationwide in 2019, but this is a combined, non-collectivity figure with no trans-only breakdown or denominator, so trans-specific prevalence is undocumented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Transphobic motive aggravates crimes punishable by imprisonment since 2017, applying here.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: The combined national figure cannot establish visitor-facing street risk in this collectivity.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Watchdog documented recurring serious violations since 2010 without a documented remedy; whether its 2021 findings were acted on in this collectivity is unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Penal-code discrimination ground and aggravating-factor provisions are documented as operative national law.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper recourse does not offset the documented custody practice where oversight findings recurred without shown correction.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.25-C: that anchor adds criminalisation enabling arrest plus birth-sex custody and solitary-as-protection. Here custody harm is documented, but no presentation offence or arrest pathway is documented, so the case is safer.

Lower than 0.55-C: that anchor centres on ward placement by document marker causing delayed or denied care. Here the marker-based placement is in prisons with assault threats and a watchdog finding of persistent serious violations, a more severe interaction.

Much lower than 0.75-C: that anchor has brief, releasable border detention with counsel and compensation. Here no border-exposure is documented, but the documented detention consequence is persistent rights violations without shown remedy, placing it well below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is nationally protective on paper but custodially exposed in practice. If a visitor is never detained, documented everyday exposure is thin. If outing leads to detention, document-to-placement interaction delivers the visitor into all-male facilities for trans women with assault threats, and the watchdog record shows successive findings without documented correction in this collectivity. That conditional, state-run harm dominates the score, producing elevated risk despite no criminalisation of trans identity.
